questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
It depends on the boot. Most Blundstones come pretreated, so I wouldn't treat those out of the box. Rustic or distressed styles are the exception, and I'd condition them. After that there's no fixed schedule: treat them when they look or feel dry.

**Out of the box**
- Blundstone's FAQ says most of their boots are pretreated and shouldn't be treated out of the box. As I read it, treating them again just makes things roll off [1].
- Rustic Brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black leathers don't carry that same pretreatment [2]. I first assumed my distressed pair was treated, and that turned out to be wrong.
- For rustic boots I recommend conditioning them, and I don't recommend leaving them dry [3]. The oil will darken them.

**How often**
- I treat mine when I feel they need it, and I probably do too little [4].
- The signs are leather that looks or feels dry, or water that no longer beads on top. Dry-looking leather needs oil, and poor beading means more wax [5].
- Clean boots regularly, because dirt wears the leather down faster [6].
- In my first review I said you may have to wax them every month, maybe every week [7]. Later I settled on going by feel instead.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, the first soak or wash in water will make them tighter, mostly in the waist, but they loosen up again with wear. They're shrink-to-fit, so putting them in the bathtub is what shrinks them [1].

**What shrinks:** After my first soak and air-dry, they definitely slimmed up, mainly around the waist [2]. The length barely changed [2].

**Sizing for it:** My rule is to go two sizes up [1]. I went the other way with a 29 waist, and I could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe at first [3]. I'd also have gotten a longer length, a 32, than the 30 I bought [3].

**Loosening afterwards:** A week later the waist and thighs had stretched enough to wear a belt [4].

**Washing them later:** Don't use very hot water or the dryer if you want a nice fit [5]. In the dryer they'd start out a lot smaller [6].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
I'd buy a 35 waist and a 32 length. My rule for the 501 STF is to go up two sizes in the waist [1] and two inches longer in length [2], so your 33x30 becomes 35x32.

- **Waist:** In my comparison I went from a 30 to a 32 for the STF, which is two sizes up [3]. The STF waist shrinks when you soak it, so the tag number comes out bigger than the finished waist [3]. I bought a 29 waist once and could barely get into them, and I couldn't breathe [4]. Sizing up two avoids that, and after you wet them they fit normally [2].
- **Length:** I wish I had bought a 32 length instead of my 30 [4]. That matches the two inches longer I recommend [2].

I haven't covered the Levi's 502 in my videos, so I can't say how its sizing compares to the 501. This is my 501 STF rule applied to your numbers, not a conversion from the 502.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
I cuff mainly because I can't settle on a hem length. I never know whether I want no break, half break or full break, and cuffing is the only fix I've found short of committing to one fit [1]. Cuffs also make your legs look shorter, which is a downside [2].

- **Style:** I cuffed my 501s because my current style doesn't suit wider-legged pants left uncuffed [3]. I'd also have bought them a size longer in the length [3].
- **Length:** For me, jeans that look too long just look bad, and that matters more to me than anything else [4].
- **Boots:** I used to always cuff, but I now like wearing jeans down over my boots more [5].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
Not as firmly as I used to. I've said the 3335s are my favorite Red Wings of all time, and they still might be, but probably not [1]. The 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics I really like [1]. The 3335s are also on the list of boots I'm getting rid of [1].

**Why I liked the 3335s more:** I like them for the stitch-down construction. They are lighter, so I feel more nimble in them, and they're easier for walking or a light hike [1]. Earlier I called them my favorite boots I've ever had, ahead of the 1907s and 875s, and a dramatically better all-around boot for hikes and walks in the woods [2]. Not long after, I still called them my favorite Red Wings to date [3].

**Where the 1907s win:** The 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so if you need a tough boot the 3335s are probably not the ones to go for [2]. Among moc toe Red Wings, I think you should get the 1907s [4].

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
Solovair comes out ahead of the made in England Docs: it's the better boot and it costs less [1]. Solovair is about $40 cheaper, so you get a better boot without the Doc Martens markup [2].

**Where Solovair wins**
- Midsoles: Solovair uses thicker, heavier, more robust felted midsoles [3].
- Shank: Solovair boots have a shank, which makes them a bit more comfortable over long periods [4].
- Repairs: Solovair sells its soles on its website, so you can resole them yourself or have them do it [5].

**Where they're about even**
- Leather: I see the made in England leather as probably on par with Solovair's [6]. Solovair does use full grain leather, though that varies by model [7].

**Where Docs still make sense**
- The yellow stitching. If it matters to you, you have to get the made in England Docs [8].
- If you're a big Doc Martens fan who wants boots made like the old ones, go made in England [9]. Purely on value, I'd say the extra $90 over the Thailand pair is probably not worth it [10].

**Solovair caveats**
- My first Solovair monkey boots had a back tab rip off [11].
- The pair they sent for review ran very big, so check sizing carefully [12].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
I wouldn't pick Blundstones as my boots for a serious hiking trip. They don't have good ankle support, so they're not good boots for mountaining [1]. They did hold up for me on hikes and a few mountains in Maine, with some scuffs [2].

I haven't covered multi-day hikes in my videos, so I can't say how they'd do over four days in a row. Here is what I can tell you:

- **Break-in:** Mine gave me big blisters when I first started running and walking the track in them, even though I thought they were broken in. That stopped after two to three weeks [3]. If yours aren't well broken in, keep that in mind.
- **Wet conditions:** Mine stayed dry enough for crossing a brook or stream, or standing in mud for a bit [4].

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
I'd go for the Muji tee. For your build, it's the better value pick than Uniqlo's $20 shirt. Uniqlo is probably the best t-shirt for the price, but if you're taller or wider, Muji is the one I'd pick [1]. It costs about $4 or $5 more, but it's significantly longer and a good deal wider [2].

**Why not Uniqlo:** the $20 Uniqlo is my starter tee and a great deal [3]. It's the shirt for average proportions, and it fits narrower and shorter than Muji [1].

**If you want to spend a bit more:** House of Blanks at $35 is combed ringspun, cut and sewn in Canada, with absolutely zero torquing, and I think it's an outstanding value [4].

**Size:** I haven't covered what size to pick for your height and weight, so I can't give you a number. What I can say is that Muji's cut is longer and wider than Uniqlo's, so you'd probably find it roomier. In a tee I like a lot of space across the shoulders [5].

I should be clear that this is my own collaboration. Separately, the Feit Classic Lows are my favorite sneakers and I wear them every day [6]. I haven't covered them as a cold-weather pick, though, so I can't say how they do in winter.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
If you're choosing a moc toe Red Wing, I'd go for the 1907 [1]. The main differences are the construction and what's included, since the 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875 [2].

**What the 1907 adds**
- It has a storm welt, which I find invaluable [3]. From what I've seen on Reddit, Red Wing's version is basically another strip of leather stitched onto the welt, though I'm not quite sure [4].
- It comes with a removable leather footbed, which you can otherwise buy separately for about $40 [3].
- It comes with leather laces, which are typically about $15 [3].

**The 875**
- It's Goodyear welted, which I think is durable and pretty water resistant [5].
- The Goodyear welt leaves room for a cork insole [5].

**What they share**
- Both have crepe soles, which I expect to break down faster than the Vibram sole on the 3335 [6].
- Both are more beefily constructed than the 3335, so they suit you better if you need a tough boot [7].

**Water resistance**
In my water test, one 1907 leaked almost immediately through the stitching [8]. I still expect them to hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [8]. Welted leather boots aren't great on water resistance in general [9].

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
For the lowest price, I'd go with Uniqlo; for the best budget shirt overall, I'd pick The Front General Store if you can stretch to about $40.

**Uniqlo.** At $20 it's probably the best t-shirt you can get for the price, bar none [1]. It's your starter tee, and it's open-end and a bit rough [2]. It has a bound neck collar that doesn't wiggle [3]. If you're taller or wider, I'd look at Muji instead, which costs a little more but is longer and wider [2].

**The Front General Store.** It's a $40, 100% made-in-Japan shirt with great proportions and feel [4]. In my most recent best-value pick I chose it over House of Blanks for today, since I like the character [5]. Earlier I called it one of the best shirts you could get, with 1.2% width shrink, 0% length shrink and 6/10 softness [6].

**Pro Club.** I like it, but it's the roughest shirt in that test, rated 4/10 for softness [7]. It also shrank 2.78% in width and 6.86% in length [7].

**Hanes.** It's a classic $10 shirt that's great for the price, rated 7/10 for softness [8]. It shrank 1.45% in width and 6.73% in length [8]. With the very cheap mass-market brands I lumped together, all five shirts I had from them showed some defect [9][10].

I haven't directly ranked Pro Club or Hanes against Uniqlo in a single video. Uniqlo wins on price and construction, and The Front General Store wins on feel and character if you'll pay double.

questions.question: Would you recommend this [Barbour Bedale] or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
I'd go with the Bedale for this mix of rain, wind and light spring use. Its rain features and all-season layering room are what I've covered in detail. I haven't said anything about the Flint and Tinder's rain performance or wind resistance, so I can't call it better for that.

**Barbour Bedale:**
- It's the lightest-weight fabric of all the waxed jackets I looked at, and it's not a designated rain jacket. That lightness is why you can wear it in any season and layer under it comfortably. [1]
- It has a throat latch and storm cuffs, which help in bad weather. [2]
- It also has a storm flap over the zipper so water doesn't run through. [3]
- A brand-new coat of wax didn't leak at all in my shower test. [4]
- Water resistance depends on the state of the wax: once the jacket is worn for a few seasons and the wax wears thin, water will come right in. Plan on re-waxing. [5]
- I highly suggest getting the snap-on hood for rain. [6]

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker:**
- It's built for everyone and goes with anything. It's a lighter weight, so it's comfortable. [7]
- It's $300, lined and made in the US, so it's hard not to recommend. [8]
- That segment was sponsored by Huckberry, though I said I'd talked about this jacket many times before the sponsorship. [9]

If you mainly want a light spring jacket, the Flint and Tinder is a good option. For rain and wind use, the Bedale has the features I've actually covered.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
The con only applies to the unlined version of the Huckberry jacket that I was testing in that video, not to the lined ones. That jacket was the cheapest, simplest, unlined one on the list [1]. My con was that I personally like a lining on waxed jackets so the wax doesn't touch your clothes or arms, and that applies to the unlined Huckberry and Rogue Territory jackets [2].

I know the lined versions exist. Huckberry offers the jacket both with and without a lining [3]. The standard lined one has a polyester lining [4], and there is also a wool-lined version, though it's made in much more limited quantity [5].

I like the lined version for exactly that reason: it's comfortable and you don't get wax on your skin. I haven't tried the wool-lined one yet [6].

My view on linings has softened a bit. I usually want a liner on a waxed jacket, but I now see why you might leave one out, since a satin-sleeve lining limits how often you can wear the jacket once it gets warm [7].

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
I haven't directly compared the fit of the 3335s to the 875s in my videos. What I can say is that I went true to size in the 3335s and they fit fine [1].

**3335 fit:** The profile is slim and the boots taper down. With thin cotton socks I had no discomfort or tightness, but with wool socks my toes felt squished and I couldn't wiggle them much [2]. If you wear thick socks, keep that in mind.

**Red Wings in general:** In my 1907 video I wear an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and they fit perfectly [3]. I like leather boots snug but not squished, because the leather is stiff at first and molds to your foot [3]. I didn't give a specific 875 fit rundown, so I can't say how its toe room compares to the 3335's.
